claim: The transcription factor Bm-mamo is responsible for black dilute (bd) allele mutations in the silkworm.
source: In this study, we found that the transcription factor Bm-mamo is responsible for black dilute (bd) allele mutations in the silkworm.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Bm-mamo belongs to the BTB zinc finger family.
source: Bm-mamo belongs to the BTB zinc finger family and is orthologous to mamo in Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by sequence analysis.

claim: Bm-mamo is orthologous to mamo in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: Bm-mamo belongs to the BTB zinc finger family and is orthologous to mamo in Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Bm-mamo has a conserved function in gamete production in Drosophila and silkworms.
source: This gene has a conserved function in gamete production in Drosophila and silkworms and has evolved a pleiotropic function in the regulation of color patterns in caterpillars.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by phenotypic observations.

claim: Bm-mamo has evolved a pleiotropic function in the regulation of color patterns in caterpillars.
source: This gene has a conserved function in gamete production in Drosophila and silkworms and has evolved a pleiotropic function in the regulation of color patterns in caterpillars.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Bm-mamo is a repressor of dark melanin patterns in the larval epidermis.
source: Using RNAi and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) technology, we showed that Bm-mamo is a repressor of dark melanin patterns in the larval epidermis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by RNAi and CRISPR experiments.

claim: Bm-mamo likely regulates the expression of related pigment synthesis and cuticular protein genes in a coordinated manner.
source: Using in vitro binding assays and gene expression profiling in wild-type and mutant larvae, we also showed that Bm-mamo likely regulates the expression of related pigment synthesis and cuticular protein genes in a coordinated manner to mediate its role in color pattern formation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by EMSA and qPCR data.

claim: Insect color patterns are involved in behavior.
source: Insects often display stunning colors, and the patterns of these colors have been shown to be involved in behavior (Sword et al., 2000), immunity (Barnes and Siva-Jothy, 2000), thermoregulation (Hadley et al., 1992), and UV protection (Hu et al., 2013); in particular, visual antagonism of predators via aposematism (Stevens and Ruxton, 2012), mimicry (Dasmahapatra, 2012), cryptic color patterns (Gaitonde et al., 2018), or some combination of the above (Tullberg et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

source: In addition, the color patterns are divergent and convergent among populations (Wittkopp et al., 2003b).

claim: Insect coloration can be pigmentary, structural, or bioluminescent.
source: Insect coloration can be pigmentary, structural, or bioluminescent.
evidence: This is stated directly as a classification of insect coloration types.

claim: Pigments are synthesized by insects themselves and form solid particles that are deposited within the cuticle of the body surface and the scales of the wings.
source: Pigments are synthesized by insects themselves and form solid particles that are deposited within the cuticle of the body surface and the scales of the wings (Futahashi et al., 2010; Matsuoka and Monteiro, 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Bile pigments and carotenoid pigments synthesized through biological synthesis are incorporated into the body fluids and fill in the wing membranes of Siproeta stelenes and Philaethria diatonica via hemolymph circulation.
source: Interestingly, recent studies have shown that bile pigments and carotenoid pigments synthesized through biological synthesis are incorporated into the body fluids and fill in the wing membranes of two butterflies (Siproeta stelenes and Philaethria diatonica) via hemolymph circulation, providing color in the form of liquid pigments (Finet et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Pigments form colors by selective absorption and/or scattering of light depending on their physical properties.
source: These pigments form colors by selective absorption and/or scattering of light depending on their physical properties (Gürses et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Structural color refers to colors generated by optical interference and grating diffraction of the microstructure/nanostructure of the body surface or appendages.
source: However, structural color refers to colors, such as metallic colors and iridescence, generated by optical interference and grating diffraction of the microstructure/nanostructure of the body surface or appendages (such as scales) (Lloyd and Nadeau, 2021; Seago et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Some insects exhibit colors in the dark due to bioluminescence.
source: However, some insects, such as fireflies, exhibit colors (green to orange) in the dark due to bioluminescence (Oba et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Bioluminescence occurs when luciferase catalyzes the oxidation of small molecules of luciferin.
source: Bioluminescence occurs when luciferase catalyzes the oxidation of small molecules of luciferin (Syed and Anderson, 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: The metabolic pathways associated with melanins, pterins, and ommochromes have been identified in Lepidoptera.
source: Recent research has identified the metabolic pathways associated with related pigments, such as melanins, pterins, and ommochromes, in Lepidoptera (Tong et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: A deficiency of enzymes in the pigment metabolism pathway can lead to changes in color patterns.
source: A deficiency of enzymes in the pigment metabolism pathway can lead to changes in color patterns (Dai et al., 2010; Wittkopp et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: The microstructure/nanostructure of the body surface and wing scales are important factors that influence body color patterns.
source: In addition to pigment synthesis, the microstructure/nanostructure of the body surface and wing scales are important factors that influence body color patterns.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: The body surface and wing scales of Lepidoptera are composed mainly of cuticular proteins (CPs).
source: The body surface and wing scales of Lepidoptera are composed mainly of cuticular proteins (CPs) (Liu et al., 2021; Yan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: In Bombyx mori, more than 220 genes encode CPs.
source: For example, in Bombyx mori, more than 220 genes encode CPs (Futahashi et al., 2008a).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

source: In addition, several pleiotropic factors, such as wnt1 (Yamaguchi et al., 2013), Apontic-like (Yoda et al., 2014), clawless (Jin et al., 2019), abdominal-A (Rogers et al., 2014), abdominal-B (Jeong et al., 2006), engrailed (Dufour et al., 2020), antennapedia (Prakash et al., 2022), optix (Reed et al., 2011), bric à brac (bab) (Kopp et al., 2000), and Distal-less (Dll) (Arnoult et al., 2013), play important roles in the regulation of color patterns.

claim: Silkworms have been completely domesticated for more than 5000 years.
source: Silkworms (B. mori) have been completely domesticated for more than 5000 years and are famous for their silk fiber production (Tong et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Approximately 200 strains of silkworm mutants with variable color patterns have been preserved.
source: Because of this long history of domestication, artificial selection, and genetic research, its genetic background has been well studied, and approximately 200 strains of mutants with variable color patterns have been preserved (Cheng. et al., 2003), which provides a good resource for color pattern research.
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: The black dilute (bd) mutant exhibits recessive Mendelian inheritance.
source: The black dilute (bd) mutant, which exhibits recessive Mendelian inheritance, has a dark gray larval body color, and the female is sterile.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: The bd mutant has a dark gray larval body color.
source: The black dilute (bd) mutant, which exhibits recessive Mendelian inheritance, has a dark gray larval body color, and the female is sterile.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bd mutant female is sterile.
source: The black dilute (bd) mutant, which exhibits recessive Mendelian inheritance, has a dark gray larval body color, and the female is sterile.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Black dilute fertile (bdf) is an allele that leads to a lighter body color than bd and fertile females.
source: Black dilute fertile (bdf) is an allele that leads to a lighter body color than bd and fertile females (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The bd and bdf mutations were mapped to a single locus at 22.9 cM of linkage group 9.
source: The two mutations were mapped to a single locus at 22.9 cM of linkage group 9 (Kawaguchi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: A genomic region of approximately 390 kb was responsible for the bd phenotype.
source: A genomic region of approximately 390 kb was responsible for the bd phenotype (Supplementary file 1–Table S1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section and supported by mapping data.

claim: The genomic region responsible for bd includes five predicted genes according to the SilkDB database.
source: According to the SilkDB database (Duan et al., 2010), this region included five predicted genes (BGIBMGA012516, BGIBMGA012517, BGIBMGA012518, BGIBMGA012519, and BGIBMGA014089).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: BGIBMGA012517 and BGIBMGA012518 were significantly downregulated on Day 3 of the fifth instar of the larvae in the bd phenotype individuals.
source: Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) was subsequently performed, which revealed that BGIBMGA012517 and BGIBMGA012518 were significantly downregulated on Day 3 of the fifth instar of the larvae in the bd phenotype individuals, while there was no difference in the expression levels of the other genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: BGIBMGA012517 and BGIBMGA012518 are predicted to be associated with a single locus (LOC101738295) in GenBank.
source: These two genes were predicted to be associated with a single locus (LOC101738295) in GenBank.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The predicted genes BGIBMGA012517 and BGIBMGA012518 were proven to be one gene by gene cloning.
source: By gene cloning, the predicted genes BGIBMGA012517 and BGIBMGA012518 were proven to be one such gene.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section and supported by cloning experiments.

claim: The 12517/8 gene produces two transcripts in the wild-type Dazao strain.
source: The 12517/8 gene produces two transcripts; the open reading frame (ORF) of the long transcript is 2397 bp, and the ORF of the short transcript is 1824 bp, which is the same 5′-terminus, in the wild-type Dazao strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ORF of the long transcript of the 12517/8 gene is 2397 bp.
source: The 12517/8 gene produces two transcripts; the open reading frame (ORF) of the long transcript is 2397 bp, and the ORF of the short transcript is 1824 bp, which is the same 5′-terminus, in the wild-type Dazao strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ORF of the short transcript of the 12517/8 gene is 1824 bp.
source: The 12517/8 gene produces two transcripts; the open reading frame (ORF) of the long transcript is 2397 bp, and the ORF of the short transcript is 1824 bp, which is the same 5′-terminus, in the wild-type Dazao strain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 12517/8 gene showed significantly lower expression in the bdf mutant.
source: The 12517/8 gene showed significantly lower expression in the bdf mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and comparative genomic analysis revealed multiple variations in the region near this gene between bdf and Dazao (Supplementary file 2–Table S2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Comparative genomic analysis revealed multiple variations in the region near the 12517/8 gene between bdf and Dazao.
source: The 12517/8 gene showed significantly lower expression in the bdf mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and comparative genomic analysis revealed multiple variations in the region near this gene between bdf and Dazao (Supplementary file 2–Table S2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by supplementary data.

claim: 12517/8 was completely silenced in the bd mutant due to the deletion of DNA fragments (approximately 168 kb) from the first upstream intron and an insertion of 3560 bp.
source: In addition, 12517/8 was completely silenced due to the deletion of DNA fragments (approximately 168 kb) from the first upstream intron and an insertion of 3560 bp in the bd mutant (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The 12517/8 gene has high sequence similarity to mamo in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: To predict the function of the 12517/8 gene, we performed a BLAST search using its full-length sequence and found a transcription factor, the maternal gene required for meiosis (mamo) in Drosophila melanogaster, that had high sequence similarity to that of the 12517/8 gene (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The mamo gene belongs to the Broad-complex, Tramtrack and bric à brac/poxvirus zinc finger protein (BTB-ZF) family.
source: The mamo gene belongs to the Broad-complex, Tramtrack and bric à brac/poxvirus zinc finger protein (BTB-ZF) family.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: In the BTB-ZF family, the zinc finger serves as a recognition motif for DNA-specific sequences.
source: In the BTB-ZF family, the zinc finger serves as a recognition motif for DNA-specific sequences, and the BTB domain promotes oligomerization and the recruitment of other regulatory factors (Bardwell and Treisman, 1994).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: The BTB domain promotes oligomerization and the recruitment of other regulatory factors.
source: In the BTB-ZF family, the zinc finger serves as a recognition motif for DNA-specific sequences, and the BTB domain promotes oligomerization and the recruitment of other regulatory factors (Bardwell and Treisman, 1994).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Most BTB-ZF factors are transcriptional repressors.
source: Most of these factors are transcriptional repressors, such as nuclear receptor corepressor (N-CoR) and silencing mediator for retinoid and thyroid hormone receptor (SMRT) (Huynh and Bardwell, 1998), but some are activators, such as p300 (Staller et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Some BTB-ZF factors are activators, such as p300.
source: Most of these factors are transcriptional repressors, such as nuclear receptor corepressor (N-CoR) and silencing mediator for retinoid and thyroid hormone receptor (SMRT) (Huynh and Bardwell, 1998), but some are activators, such as p300 (Staller et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: mamo is enriched in embryonic primordial germ cells in D. melanogaster.
source: mamo is enriched in embryonic primordial germ cells in D. melanogaster.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Individuals deficient in mamo are able to undergo oogenesis but fail to execute meiosis properly, leading to female infertility in D. melanogaster.
source: Individuals deficient in mamo are able to undergo oogenesis but fail to execute meiosis properly, leading to female infertility in D. melanogaster (Mukai et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: Bm-mamo gene was highly expressed in the molting stage of caterpillars.
source: The gene was highly expressed in the molting stage of caterpillars, and its expression was upregulated in the later pupal and adult stages (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: Bm-mamo expression was upregulated in the later pupal and adult stages.
source: The gene was highly expressed in the molting stage of caterpillars, and its expression was upregulated in the later pupal and adult stages (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: The Bm-mamo gene responds to ecdysone and participates in the processes of molting and metamorphosis in silkworms.
source: This finding suggested that the Bm-mamo gene responds to ecdysone and participates in the processes of molting and metamorphosis in silkworms.
evidence: This is inferred from the expression pattern data.

claim: In 5th-instar 3rd-day larvae, the midgut, head, and epidermis exhibited high expression levels of Bm-mamo.
source: According to the investigation of tissue-specific Dazao strain expression in 5th-instar 3rd-day larvae, the midgut, head, and epidermis exhibited high expression levels; the trachea, nerves, silk glands, testis, ovary, muscle, wing disc, and Malpighian tubules exhibited moderate expression levels; and the blood and fat bodies exhibited low expression levels (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: Bm-mamo is involved in the regulation of the development of multiple silkworm tissues.
source: These findings suggested that Bm-mamo is involved in the regulation of the development of multiple silkworm tissues.
evidence: This is inferred from the tissue-specific expression data.

claim: In the epidermis, the Bm-mamo gene was upregulated during the molting period, and the highest expression was observed at the beginning of molting.
source: In the epidermis, the Bm-mamo gene was upregulated during the molting period, and the highest expression was observed at the beginning of molting (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: Bm-mamo deficiency can cause melanin pigmentation.
source: We found significant melanin pigmentation in the epidermis of the newly molted 5th-instar larvae. These findings indicate that Bm-mamo deficiency can cause melanin pigmentation (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by RNAi experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The melanistic phenotype of the RNAi individuals was similar to that of the bd mutants.
source: The melanistic phenotype of the RNAi individuals was similar to that of the bd mutants.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: Gene-edited individuals had a significantly melanistic body color.
source: The gene-edited individuals had a significantly melanistic body color, and the female moths were sterile (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 5.

claim: Gene-edited Bm-mamo knockout female moths were sterile.
source: The gene-edited individuals had a significantly melanistic body color, and the female moths were sterile (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 5.

claim: The Bm-mamo gene negatively regulates melanin pigmentation in caterpillars.
source: These results indicated that the Bm-mamo gene negatively regulates melanin pigmentation in caterpillars and participates in the reproductive regulation of female moths.
evidence: This is stated directly as a conclusion from the functional experiments.

claim: Bm-mamo participates in the reproductive regulation of female moths.
source: These results indicated that the Bm-mamo gene negatively regulates melanin pigmentation in caterpillars and participates in the reproductive regulation of female moths.
evidence: This is stated directly as a conclusion from the functional experiments.

claim: The amino acid residues of the zinc finger motif of the mamo-S protein were highly conserved among 57 species.
source: Sequence alignment revealed that the amino acid residues of the zinc finger motif of the mamo-S protein were highly conserved among 57 species.
evidence: This is stated directly in the Results section.

claim: The DNA-binding sequence of mamo (TGCGT) in Drosophila was confirmed by electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA).
source: In addition, the DNA-binding sequence of mamo (TGCGT) in Drosophila was confirmed by electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) (Hira et al., 2013), which has a consensus sequence with the predicted binding site sequence of Bm-mamo-S (GTGCGTGGC), and the predicted sequence was longer.
evidence: This is stated directly with citation support.

claim: The predicted DNA-binding sites of Bm-mamo-L and Bm-mamo-S were highly consistent with those of mamo orthologs in different species.
source: Furthermore, the predicted DNA-binding sites of Bm-mamo-L and Bm-mamo-S were highly consistent with those of mamo orthologs in different species (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The mamo protein may regulate similar target genes between species.
source: This finding suggested that the protein may regulate similar target genes between species.
